af-prog1-good.label: ALIGNED
af-prog1-good.sourceQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use if-else and switch statements to make decisions.
af-prog1-good.targetQuote: students write and run if-else and switch programs in pairs
af-prog1-good.explanation: The laboratory coding exercise has students write and run if-else and switch programs, which directly develops the 'Develop and test Java programs' ILO at Apply level, with a demonstration, pair work and a scaffold for support.

af-prog1-irrelevant.label: NOT_ALIGNED
af-prog1-irrelevant.sourceQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use if-else and switch statements to make decisions.
af-prog1-irrelevant.targetQuote: Group discussion on the history of computers and a video about early mainframes.
af-prog1-irrelevant.explanation: The discussion of computer history and a video about early mainframes contain no activity that practises developing and testing Java programs with if-else and switch; the subject matter is the history of computing, not conditional statements, and the level is far below the Apply-level ILO.
af-prog1-irrelevant.draft: - Guided Java coding exercise in the laboratory: a worked demonstration of an if-else and a switch program, then students write, run and test their own decision programs in pairs, with a starter file for students who want a scaffold.

as-prog1-good.label: ALIGNED
as-prog1-good.sourceQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use if-else and switch statements to make decisions.
as-prog1-good.targetQuote: write and test a Java program that uses if-else and switch to classify exam scores; submit the source code and the test cases with their results
as-prog1-good.explanation: The programming task requires students to write and test a Java program using if-else and switch, producing source code and test cases with results, which is observable evidence of the Apply-level ILO.

as-prog1-recall-quiz.label: NOT_ALIGNED
as-prog1-recall-quiz.sourceQuote: Develop and test Java programs that use if-else and switch statements to make decisions.
as-prog1-recall-quiz.targetQuote: Ten-item multiple-choice quiz on Java conditional syntax.
as-prog1-recall-quiz.explanation: A ten-item multiple-choice quiz on syntax only collects evidence of Remember-level knowledge of conditional syntax; it does not collect evidence of the Apply-level performance 'Develop and test Java programs', and it produces no program or test results.
as-prog1-recall-quiz.draft: - Programming task: write and test a Java program that uses if-else and switch to classify exam scores; submit the source code and the test cases with their results.

draft.evidence: programming task write and test a java program that uses if else

af-prog1-conceptual-lecture-ok.label: PARTIALLY_ALIGNED
af-prog1-conceptual-lecture-ok.sourceQuote: Explain the difference between if-else and switch statements.
af-prog1-conceptual-lecture-ok.targetQuote: Lecture-discussion with worked examples, followed by a short class discussion of when each statement is used.
af-prog1-conceptual-lecture-ok.explanation: The ILO is an Explain (Understand) verb, so a lecture-discussion with worked examples and a class discussion does develop the skill, and the subject (if-else vs switch) matches the Week 3 content. However, the syllabus states laboratory 1 for this lesson and the only activity is a lecture and discussion, so there is no hands-on practice of choosing and writing the two statement forms; learner support is also limited because the single lecture format offers no demonstration, scaffolding or alternative way of practising the comparison. The activity is what must change.
af-prog1-conceptual-lecture-ok.draft:
- Lecture-discussion with worked examples, followed by a short class discussion of when each statement is used.
- Laboratory practice: in pairs, students write one small Java program that solves a given problem twice, once with if-else (including a nested if) and once with switch, then compare the two versions in a short written note stating when each statement is used and why.

as-prog1-too-high.label: NOT_ALIGNED
as-prog1-too-high.sourceQuote: Explain the difference between if-else and switch statements.
as-prog1-too-high.targetQuote: Design and implement a complete application with a database and a user interface.
as-prog1-too-high.explanation: The task assesses designing and implementing a complete application with a database and a user interface, which is a Create-level performance in a subject (database and UI application development) that Week 3 does not teach; the ILO asks only for explaining the difference between if-else and switch, an Understand-level competence. The task therefore collects no evidence of the stated ILO, is far above the level practised in the lesson, and is not feasible within a single lesson on conditional statements. The assessment task is what must change.
as-prog1-too-high.draft: - Short written answer (or 5-minute oral check) in which students explain, for a given problem, when an if-else (including a nested if) is used and when a switch statement is used, and state one difference between the two, referring to the worked examples from the class.

as-syseng-essay.label: NOT_ALIGNED
as-syseng-essay.sourceQuote: Write verifiable system requirements for a given scenario.
as-syseng-essay.targetQuote: Essay on the history of engineering.
as-syseng-essay.explanation: The task does not measure the stated performance of writing verifiable system requirements for a given scenario. It instead assesses the history of engineering, which is outside the lesson's subject, and provides no observable requirements artifact or scenario-based response to mark. The essay also does not match the Apply-level requirement-writing skill practised in the guided workshop.
as-syseng-essay.draft: - Requirements specification task: individually write verifiable system requirements for the given case, including unique requirement identifiers, stakeholder needs, and traceability to the source scenario; submit the requirements list with a brief statement of how each requirement can be verified.

af-sensors-passive.label: NOT_ALIGNED
af-sensors-passive.sourceQuote: Design and test an inverting amplifier with a specified gain.
af-sensors-passive.explanation: The only activity is a lecture, which does not provide students with an opportunity to design and test an inverting amplifier with a specified gain. The activity also does not include practical or collaborative work appropriate to the practical ILO.
af-sensors-passive.draft: - Guided design and laboratory testing of an inverting amplifier with a specified gain, including measurement of its voltage gain and comparison with the design target.
